name: The Execution Fields
lesson: Process trees: spotting odd parent/child relationships, decoding encoded PowerShell, and pivoting from a process to its network activity.
pivot_tip: Pivot on the parent field. Office apps almost never have a reason to launch a shell.
reaction: updchk.exe just rotated its sleep timer. VELVET LOCUST felt the SOC move.

e201.title: EDR alert: Office spawned PowerShell
lines: ALERT  : Suspicious child process of Office application   Severity: HIGH
e201.tip: Word spawning PowerShell with a hidden window and an encoded command is one of the most reliable phishing execution signals.

e202.title: EDR process tree: WS-FIN-0142
lines: updchk.exe: unsigned, first seen 09:14:58, prevalence 1 host in the fleet
e202.tip: Prevalence of 1 means one machine in the whole company has ever run this file. Rare is suspicious.

e203.title: Proxy log: cdn.halcyon-support.test
e203.tip: A PowerShell user agent fetching a .bin from an uncategorized look-alike domain is a download cradle.

e204.title: Script Block Log (4104): decoded command
lines: [inert training sample: domains are fictional and unreachable]
e204.tip: Script Block Logging records the decoded script even when the command line was encoded. Turn it on everywhere.

e205.title: Lab note: reading process trees
lines: Encoded commands are UTF-16LE Base64. The terminal's decode handles that.
e205.tip: Know the normal parent for each process. Then anything else stands out.

proc.description: Process creation (Sysmon Event 1), finance and engineering hosts

objectives.title: Read the EDR alert
hints: Mira's workstation is a node in this zone.
Find WS-FIN-0142 and press E.
Open 'EDR alert: Office spawned PowerShell'.

objectives.title: Find the odd parent/child pair
objectives.desc: Hunt for PowerShell launched by Word.
objectives.solution: search proc where parent="winword.exe" and name="powershell.exe"
objectives.success: There it is: Word launched PowerShell.
hints: You want rows where the parent is Word AND the process is PowerShell.
Two conditions joined with 'and'.
search proc where parent="winword.exe" and name="powershell.exe"

objectives.title: Decode the hidden command
objectives.desc: The -Enc argument is Base64. Decode it: decode base64 p-202 (decode can read a row by its id).
objectives.success: Decoded: a download cradle pulling updchk.exe from a look-alike domain.
hints: The terminal's decode command can take a row id instead of the raw text.
PowerShell encodes commands as UTF-16LE Base64; decode handles it.
decode base64 p-202

objectives.title: What did PowerShell launch?
objectives.desc: Pivot: find processes whose parent was PowerShell on WS-FIN-0142.
objectives.solution: search proc where parent="powershell.exe" and host="WS-FIN-0142"
hints: Now the PowerShell process becomes the parent.
IT admins run PowerShell scripts on IT-ADM-03 too, so filter by host.
search proc where parent="powershell.exe" and host="WS-FIN-0142"

objectives.title: Where did it call out?
objectives.desc: Pivot to the network table: which connections did powershell.exe make?
objectives.success: 203.0.113.66 via cdn.halcyon-support.test. Note it: you'll see that IP again.
hints: The net table also has a 'name' field for the process.
Filter the net table on the PowerShell process name.
search net where name="powershell.exe"

objectives.title: Corroborate
objectives.desc: Collect the EDR process tree and the proxy log.
hints: Two nodes left with key evidence: the EDR console and the proxy.
Press E at EDR-CON and PROXY-01.
Open the process tree and the proxy log.

objectives.title: Rebuild the execution timeline
objectives.desc: Press L. Drag the events into the order they happened, then press C to check.

events.label: Mira opens Invoice_Q3_8841.docm and enables content

objectives.success: Timeline holds: delivery, user execution, script, download, payload, check-in.
hints: Causality: something has to be downloaded before it can run.
The email comes first, the check-in last.
Delivered, opened, PowerShell, download, updchk.exe runs, check-in.

objectives.title: Form a hypothesis
objectives.desc: Press B. Pin the proof and choose what happened.
objectives.prompt: What happened in the Execution Fields?

options.text: Mira opened the document and its macro ran hidden, encoded PowerShell that downloaded and launched a second-stage payload
An IT admin ran a patch script on Mira's machine
options.feedback: IT scripts run from IT-ADM-03 and aren't launched by Word with hidden encoded commands.

options.text: Windows Update downloaded a legitimate update
options.feedback: Windows Update doesn't run from Word or use halcyon-support.test.

options.text: The attacker logged in remotely and ran PowerShell
options.feedback: The parent is WINWORD.EXE. This started with the user opening the file.

hints: Pin the EDR alert and the decoded script block log.
Who started the chain: a person opening a file, or a remote login?
Pin e201 and e204, then choose the macro / PowerShell option.

objectives.title: Map it to ATT&CK
objectives.desc: Press M and map both findings.
hints: Both findings are about getting code to run.
Execution column: User Execution and Command and Scripting Interpreter.
f1 -> T1204.002 Malicious File; f2 -> T1059.001 PowerShell (both Execution).

objectives.title: Respond
objectives.desc: Press R. Preserve evidence, then contain the payload.
hints: Volatile evidence disappears when you kill processes.
Capture memory before killing updchk.exe.
Memory image, kill updchk.exe, block the domain/IP, blocklist the hash.

f1.text: Mira opened the macro-enabled attachment and enabled content
f1.hint: The user had to open the file for anything to happen.

f2.text: Word launched hidden, encoded PowerShell that downloaded updchk.exe
f2.hint: Which interpreter ran the encoded command?

responses.label: Capture a memory image of WS-FIN-0142
responses.description: Use EDR to grab a full RAM image before touching anything.
responses.tradeoff: Takes a few minutes. Preserves decoded configs, keys, and injected code.
responses.feedback: Memory captured. updchk.exe's config (C2: stat-sync.example) is in there.

responses.label: Kill the updchk.exe process
responses.tradeoff: Stops it now, but anything only in memory is lost.
responses.too_early: Killing it first destroys what's only in memory: decoded config, C2 keys. Capture memory first.

responses.label: Block cdn.halcyon-support.test and 203.0.113.66 at the proxy
responses.description: Deny the download domain and its IP for every host.
responses.tradeoff: Low risk; cheap for them to change, but stops reinfection from this lure.

responses.label: Add updchk.exe's SHA-256 to the EDR blocklist
responses.description: Prevent the exact file from running anywhere.
responses.tradeoff: Bottom of the Pyramid of Pain, but free and instant.

responses.label: Reimage WS-FIN-0142 immediately
responses.description: Wipe and reinstall Mira's workstation now.
responses.tradeoff: Destroys all evidence before you know the scope.
responses.feedback: Too early. Wiping destroys the evidence and tells them you've found this foothold, before you know what else they touched.

responses.label: Disable PowerShell on every computer in the company
responses.description: Push a policy blocking powershell.exe everywhere.
responses.tradeoff: Breaks IT automation; attackers have other interpreters.
responses.feedback: IT's patching and inventory scripts just broke. Prefer logging, Constrained Language Mode, and blocking Office child processes.

puzzle.title: CTF Cache: Execution Fields
puzzle.clue: Two hex digits per character. Try: decode hex cache
